title: Module 7 assessment
subtitle: Data Cleaning, Pivot Tables & Analysis
description: Fifteen questions across the whole of Module 7. Every question explains its answer, right or wrong.

questions.question: A formula returns #REF!. What happened?
questions.explanation: #REF! means the reference no longer exists - usually a deleted row, column or sheet. It is the one error you cannot fix by correcting inputs, because the formula has lost the information about what it pointed at.

questions.question: ##### means the formula is broken.
questions.explanation: It means the column is too narrow to display the value, or a date has gone negative. Widen the column and it resolves - it is a display state, not an error.

questions.question: Why is Remove Duplicates risky on a selection of two columns from a six-column table?
options: It deletes whole rows based only on the columns you selected, discarding differences in the others
It only removes the first duplicate
questions.explanation: Two rows identical in name and department but different in salary count as duplicates, and one is deleted. Work on a copy, and select every column that makes a record unique.

questions.question: Flash Fill updates automatically when the source data changes.
questions.explanation: Flash Fill writes static values once - change the source and the output stays as it was. Use it for a one-off clean-up; use formulas where the result must stay in step.

questions.question: A column has blanks that should repeat the value above, across 4,000 rows. What is the fast route?
options: Select the column, Go To Special > Blanks, type = and the cell above, then Ctrl+Enter
questions.explanation: Go To Special selects every blank at once, and Ctrl+Enter commits the relative formula into all of them. It is a four-second job that people often do by hand for an hour.

questions.question: The four zones of a pivot table are Filters, Columns, Rows and which?
questions.explanation: Values is where the numbers go, and what you drop there determines whether you get a sum, a count or something else. A text field dropped into Values counts rather than sums, which is a useful trick and an occasional surprise.

questions.question: A pivot table updates automatically when its source data changes.
questions.explanation: It reads from a cached snapshot and needs a refresh - Ctrl+Alt+F5 for all. A dashboard that looks stale usually just has not been refreshed, which is why a Last Refreshed stamp is worth adding.

questions.question: Why can a pivot calculated field give a wrong margin percentage?
options: It applies the formula to the summed values, not row by row
questions.explanation: A calculated field sums revenue, sums cost, then divides - which is right for a margin but wrong for anything averaging a ratio, and badly wrong for Units x Price. Calculate in the source Table instead.

questions.question: Write a formula that divides B2 by C2 and shows a dash instead of #DIV/0! when C2 is zero.
questions.explanation: IFERROR is right here because any error in a simple division is a data problem you want hidden consistently. On a lookup you would prefer IFNA, so a genuine #REF! still shows.

questions.question: Text to Columns with Delimited and then Finish is a common trick for what, besides splitting?
options: Forcing text-numbers and text-dates to convert to real values
questions.explanation: Running it on a single column with no delimiter makes Excel re-parse each cell, converting text that looks numeric into numbers. It is the fastest bulk fix for an imported column that will not sum.

questions.question: You need monthly totals from a column of daily dates in a pivot. Group the dates, or add a Month column to the source?
options: Group the dates in the pivot - it is quicker
Add a Month column to the source - it is explicit, portable and survives version differences
Use a separate pivot per month
questions.explanation: Grouping is quicker and lives inside the pivot, so it is invisible to anyone reading the source and behaves differently across Excel versions. A column in the source is visible, testable and reusable by other pivots.

questions.question: What does GETPIVOTDATA give you that a direct cell reference does not?
options: A reference by field name, which survives the pivot changing shape
questions.explanation: Point a dashboard tile at =B7 and it breaks silently the moment the pivot gains a row. GETPIVOTDATA asks for the field by name, so it either finds it or errors - which is the behaviour you want.

questions.question: You need the discount rate that makes a quote total exactly 500,000. One input, one target. Which tool?
questions.explanation: Goal Seek is built for exactly this - one changing cell, one target value. Scenario Manager compares whole sets of inputs; Solver handles multiple variables with constraints.

questions.question: A six-point check on new data should include looking for text-numbers, text-dates, trailing spaces, duplicates, blanks and inconsistent spellings.
questions.explanation: Running it before you build anything costs ten minutes and saves rebuilding a model on data that turns out to be dirty. Inconsistent spellings are the one people skip, and 'North' against 'north ' breaks every grouping.

questions.question: Find & Replace with 'Match entire cell contents' unticked, replacing 'HR' with 'People', will also change what?
options: 'CHRIS' and 'THRESHOLD', because it matches inside words
questions.explanation: Without that tick, Excel replaces the fragment wherever it appears. Preview with Find All first - the damage is quiet and spread across the sheet.
